svg.title: Radiation parameterization: algorithm flow
svg.desc: Common inputs (solar geometry, atmospheric profiles, clouds and surface) are converted into layer column amounts. The shortwave branch splits sunlight into two bands, computes gas and cloud transmittances, layer reflectances and transmittances, and combines the layers with the adding method into interface fluxes. The longwave branch converts temperature into blackbody flux, computes clear-sky and cloud transmittances between levels, the directional emission of non-isothermal layers and the interface fluxes. The two net downward fluxes are combined, and their divergence across each layer gives the radiative heating rate.
svg.text: Convert mixing ratios into layer column amounts
then give the effective path amounts:

Net downward fluxes: combine SW and LW
Flux convergence heats or cools each layer
Outputs: up/down fluxes at every interface, TOA and surface
